claims.statement: M5 is the final W3 acceptance: the DSS runs continuously online for 5 calendar days in the intranet production environment, with the main gate of 5h-anchor prediction accuracy at ±10%, plus alert behavior and stream-cut breaker checks; the acceptance code baseline is branch w4-dual-ring @ 0544fff (W4 dual-ring closeout + W4.4h), and the unmerged main branch does not affect deployment because the intranet only sees code content and versions are recorded by commit hash.

The intranet environment has no agent, so all M5 operations are performed manually against the runbook docs/09-M5内网在线验收运行手册.md (v1.0, 2026-09-29); the only automated deliverables are the acceptance scoring script spike_w3/04_m5_acceptance.py (14 unit tests + real-DB smoke verified 2026-09-29, end-to-end re-verified 2026-10-07 after the W4 change) and the d0_check.py pre-flight script.

The M5 run path has 5 stages: Stage 0 public-network preparation (half day: archive code by commit, prepare a real forward-looking week plan CSV, pick 5 days avoiding line-stop/maintenance/rest weeks), D0 intranet deployment (half day), D1–D5 continuous online run with one startup (≈10 min manual checks per day), and one-hour closeout scoring; planned rest days are automatically excluded from the acceptance scope.

Standing red lines for the whole M5 run: read-only access to the ods/dim/fct/mart/meta layers with products written only to the dss layer; no DSS_* parameter may be changed during the 5 days (any change voids the acceptance); a stream cut must not kill the process (wait for RTO ≤1h recovery and record the span); and output/snapshots/m5/ must not be deleted because it is the audit trail.

d0_check.py (run as D:\dss\env\python.exe d0_check.py on the intranet deployment machine, session set to Asia/Shanghai) performs two checks: (1) DB connectivity + ETL liveness computed as now minus MAX("DATE_EVT") of ods.carbody_history, with the original interpretation threshold <5min = normal / >30min = do not start, contact the intranet data owner; (2) a dss schema table inventory, where after the learning-table build the 13 mandatory tables should all be present.

The D0 .env is copied from .env.example and only 4 places may be edited: the DSS_DB_HOST/PORT/NAME/USER/PASSWORD block (the intranet production DB, requiring CREATE on the dss schema plus SELECT on the ods layer), DSS_PLAN_FOLDER (the acceptance-week plan CSV directory), DSS_RUN_TAG=m5 (all 5-day snapshots land in the same output/snapshots/m5/ directory), and optionally DSS_SNAPSHOT_DIR (kept at default). The agy blocking fix F1 (2026-09-29) made DSS_DB_* actually honored by the connection layer: spike_w1/common.py::_dsn() resolves DSS_DB_* over the 127.0.0.1 development defaults and connect() re-resolves it on every call.

All other .env values are production defaults that must stay untouched during M5 (changing any = acceptance void), including DSS_CLOCK_MODE=wall_clock, DSS_POLL_INTERVAL_SEC=300, DSS_STALE_MIN=30, DSS_ALPHA_MODE=off, DSS_ALERT_RED=-0.10, DSS_ALERT_YELLOW=-0.05, DSS_ALERT_DEBOUNCE_MIN=10, the 2026-04-14→08-15 learning window, DSS_DUAL_RING=1, DSS_USE_NET_DELAY=1 and DSS_SHIFT_TIER_DELAY=0.

The production dss layer starts empty, so D0[3] must rebuild the learning tables via spike_w1/01_learn_takt.py and spike_w2/01_learn_v2.py, producing 14 tables (6 W1 dim_*, 6 W2 v2_*, the mandatory W4.2c dim_expected_delay, and the optional W4.4h dim_expected_delay_shift whose absence does not block startup and falls back to shared rows); dim_weekly_plan is the 15th table and is auto-created by 01 boot plus loaded from DSS_PLAN_FOLDER. The startup existence checklist DSS_DIM_TABLES in spike_w3/01_boot_online.py lists the 14 mandatory tables and deliberately excludes dim_expected_delay_shift.

The D0[5] trial run of 01_boot_online must pass six checks before D1: all 14 dss tables present (shift table flagged but non-blocking), week plan loaded with every acceptance week day present, 120h bootstrap complete with cross_check ≤ 1%, guard = FRESH (not STALE), first console frame output, and output/snapshots/m5/ starting to receive snapshots; the trial is then stopped with Ctrl+C and the real run waits for D1.

D1–D5 run 01_boot_online.py once inside a PowerShell auto-restart loop that relaunches the process 30 seconds after a crash (state is rebuilt by the 120h bootstrap), logging per day as m5\log_YYYYMMDD.log; two encoding pitfalls measured intranet 2026-10-08 require PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 (GBK redirection of ✓/✗/⚠ crashes with UnicodeEncodeError) and cmd '>' redirection instead of PowerShell's '*>' (PS5.1 decodes subprocess UTF-8 as GBK and bakes mojibake into the log).

Wall-clock mode is 5-minute grid-aligned with drift compensation: 01_boot_online.next_grid_wait() is a pure function that sleeps to the next epoch 5-minute grid point (floor 1.0s) instead of a bare sleep(poll), so snapshot frame ts minutes always land on :00/:05/.../:55 and the M5 anchor frames can be matched with the ±3min tolerance; only the first frame (startup moment) may be unaligned, with later frames auto-aligned. One day yields 288 snapshots (one per 5-min round).

The daily ~10-minute checklist during D1–D5 records four things into three templates: process alive (before 04:45, from fresh status lines in the log), the two anchor frames (day-shift anchor follows the shift type 11h→10:00 / 10h→11:00 / 8h→13:00, mid fixed 21:30 — A/pred/target/Δ/lamp color hand-copied as double insurance), confirmed red/yellow alerts (time + shift + gap count into the alert ledger), and STALE spans (start = first STALE status line, recovery = back to FRESH, into the outage record without killing the process or touching ETL); the next morning the day's snapshot count must equal 288.

The two-stage ETL SLA (拍板 2026-09-23): development phase (public network) uses user-synced snapshots with on-demand syncing and no RTO, with offline (shadow replay) acceptance done on the public network; production phase (intranet live connection) has link failures handled by the intranet data owner role with RTO ≤ 1h, and stream-cut windows' predictions/warnings are tallied separately and excluded from the acceptance gate. Runtime behavior during the blind (stale-frozen) window is backstopped by the B3 freshness breaker (STALE freeze alert + banner).

M5 closeout is one command: conda run --no-capture-output -n paint-dss python spike_w3\04_m5_acceptance.py with --snap-dir output\snapshots\m5 and comma-separated --dates, producing output/w3-M5-验收报告.md (main table + outage stats + alert ledger + final verdict) and output/w3-M5-验收.json (machine-readable); the script is read-only with zero DB writes (SELECT only) and writes only local MD/JSON.

The M5 main gate is per workday per shift: |Δactual| ≤ 10% (--tol default 0.10) at the 5h anchor, where Δactual = (pred − actual final)/actual final and the actual final is a closed-interval count of product cars (BODY_ID LIKE '78202%') at the 4 exit stations K3IS140/1J440RB/K2IS075/K1IS135: day shift [D 04:45, D 16:30], mid shift [D 16:30, D+1 MID_END_TIMES[type]] (11h→04:00 / 10h→03:00 / 8h→01:00), same source as a_of '<=end'.

The 5h anchor frame is work_start+5h and follows the day-shift type (agy blocking fix F5: 11h→05:00 start→anchor 10:00 / 10h→06:00→11:00 / 8h→08:00→13:00; mid fixed 16:30 start→anchor 21:30); pick_anchor selects among that day's same-kind candidate frames the one closest to the anchor moment within ±3min (ANCHOR_TOL_SEC = 180), and a candidate beyond tolerance is treated as an anchor frame miss rather than a mismatched pick.

Every acceptance row falls into exactly one of four mutually exclusive reason buckets counted separately in the report (buckets sum + gated rows = total rows): gated (counted in the gate), actual_zero (actual final = 0, rest/line-stop/no events, not gated), stale (anchor frame guard.status=STALE stream-cut freeze, not gated and taking priority over gated/actual_zero), and anchor_missing (process offline / missing frame / drift beyond tolerance, an explicit trace row, never silently skipped); rest days (day-shift anchor frame has no shift / planned rest) are excluded from the gate and listed in a note.

M5 closeout supports multi-directory snapshot merging: --snap-dir can be repeated (e.g. m5 plus a legacy m5-r2) with duplicate same-ts frames resolved first-writer-wins plus a duplicate count in the report header; unlisted sibling -rN snapshot directories sharing the prefix are explicitly WARNING-named by find_sibling_run_dirs to prevent silent under-collection. With an explicit DSS_RUN_TAG, dashboard.resolve_run_tag idempotently appends to the same directory on restart (agy blocking fix F3, filenames carry timestamps so no collision), so -rN splits only occur with legacy auto-tag runs.

Stream-cut windows (guard.status=STALE rounds) are tallied separately in the M5 report — round count, total minutes (5min/round), and merged contiguous spans extended to the next round after the last STALE round — and are excluded from the acceptance gate per the 2026-09-23 ETL SLA decision; the final verdict PASS requires every gated shift row to satisfy |Δactual| ≤ 10%.

Three manual cross-checks lie outside the 04 script: (1) fill the post-hoc verification column of the alert ledger (gap truly occurred = valid alert, did not occur = false alarm; only confirmed transitions with the 10-minute debounce enter the ledger, same source as 03/M10), (2) outage spans must match the data owner's ETL fault records, and (3) daily snapshot count must equal 288 (a missing frame means the process was down; check the corresponding log).

Oven-channel storage dead vehicles are a known false-positive class excluded from the acceptance gate and counted separately (decision 2026-10-05 D8 option (a), no code or red-line parameter change): when the oven is closed in heating-off state, 16IS/18IS channels act as temporary storage so cars can linger; full-history measurement (16,815 vehicle-times) shows 47 above the 120h dead-vehicle threshold (0.28%) with a maximum of 190.4h. The 04 scoring consumes only the 5h anchor Δactual so dead-vehicle entries do not enter the verdict, and the mechanism is safe because the linger occurs before oven exit (the first_oven anchor and passed_oven state are unaffected).

tests/test_w3_m5_acceptance.py holds 21 unit tests covering the 04 scoring logic: type-following day anchors (F5), ±180s anchor tolerance (F2), the mutually exclusive four-bucket reasons (F4), type-dependent actual-final closed intervals, stale span merging and multi-directory merging / -rN warnings; the agy first-round blocking fixes F1–F5 (DSN env override, grid alignment, explicit-tag idempotency, structured reasons, type-based anchors) all landed in 04 and the online path with 297/297 tests green (2026-09-29).

DSS_DUAL_RING is a strict 1/0 gate (invalid values raise at startup) that selects the engine: default 1 = the W4 Doc14 unified dual-ring state-machine engine (production default, W4.3d / D6 decision) and 0 = the legacy estimate_event path (W1/W2 original semantics), i.e. a 30-second rollback. The consumption point spike_w2/eta_v2.py::dual_ring_enabled() re-reads the environment variable on every call; the DSSConfig.dual_ring field is only a mirror for the startup-report echo.

True rollback of the old engine stack is DSS_DUAL_RING=0 AND DSS_USE_NET_DELAY=0; the combination DUAL_RING=0 AND ND=1 is a half-migration degraded state (measured 2026-10-07 in W4.4f: W2 sc3 11.00% / W3 M9 α=off 11.99%, both failing against baselines) and must not be used as a rollback.

The rollback precedent verified at the W4 closeout (2026-10-07): switching DSS_DUAL_RING=0 produced 288/288 zero diff — a full 24h/288-step status-line sequence byte-identical to the baseline — and this rollback semantics is reference-only for troubleshooting and forbidden during the acceptance window (changing any DSS_* parameter voids M5).

Per the user decision of 2026-09-20, agents never execute git commit: all commits are performed by the user, and an agent only reports the changed-file list plus a suggested commit message when a task or wave completes, for the user to verify and commit.

The wave closeout flow is: user commits the code → the BM thread note is appended with this wave's decisions/measured results → CHANGELOG.md (wave-level granularity, written at closeout rather than per commit; design decisions/wording/pitfalls go to the BM note) → Pi initiates openwiki update → the file list and suggested commit message are reported → user commits.

The docs/09 troubleshooting quick table has 7 items: missing-table startup error (re-run 01_learn_takt / 01_learn_v2), week-plan missing days (fix the CSV against plan_inbox/README.md and re-run 01 with idempotent upsert), persistent STALE (ETL cut, not a DSS fault — record the span, contact the data owner, auto-thaws on recovery, not gated meanwhile), cross_check > 1% (inspect the boot report details; if the bootstrap data itself is bad, contact the data owner), repeated process restarts (check the tail stack of m5\log_*.log; usually a dropped DB connection that the restart loop self-heals), missing snapshot frames (process was offline at that time; the span appears as anchor-missing rows in the closeout report), and '段=待确认' in frames (85 un-mapped station sections, M3 open item — non-blocking).

The 04 acceptance script is deliberately aligned with the existing calibration and must not be changed: 4 exit stations via spike_w3/common.EXIT_STATIONS (K3IS140/1J440RB/K2IS075/K1IS135), product cars BODY_ID LIKE '78202%', SET TIME ZONE 'Asia/Shanghai' on every query, mid-shift end by type via spike_w2/shifts.MID_END_TIMES, the 5h anchor via spike_w2/shifts.DAY_TYPES/MID_START, and the alert ledger limited to confirmed (10-minute debounced) transitions, same source as 03/M10.
